messages:
Maria Chen: FYI AcmeOps reported their invoice is ~12% higher than the dashboard shows. They run the private meter agent (v1.4.2) in a VPC with intermittent NAT gateways.
Devon R.: when did they first see the delta?
Maria Chen: billing period started 2026-02-01. They alerted yesterday after the invoice posted. Dashboard token totals for that period are ~1.03M but invoice shows 1.15M.
Devon R.: ok. can we get agent logs and agent_id? also any recent agent updates?
Maria Chen: agent_id=agent-7b3c, running on prem VM. No planned updates since Jan. Attached logs (trimmed) below.
Maria Chen: ```
2026-02-12T20:59:50Z INFO  meter-agent starting flush cycle
2026-02-12T21:03:04Z WARN  buffer_flush failed write: no space left on device
2026-02-12T21:03:04Z INFO  heartbeat sent=2026-02-12T21:03:04Z
2026-02-12T21:03:05Z ERROR persistent_queue drop_event id=... reason=ttl_expired age=35m
2026-02-12T21:03:06Z INFO  reconnecting to control-plane
```
Devon R.: disk full + ttl_expired looks suspicious. meter-agent-bot, did we fire any alerts for agent-7b3c?
meter-agent-bot: ALERT agent-7b3c: buffer_disk_util > 95% and missed_heartbeat_count=3 :warning:
Oncall SRE: pinged customer to confirm whether they had local disk rotation or ephemeral mounts.
Kevin Liu: also check clock sync. TTL-based drops + disk full can cause events to be dropped if timestamps are older than retention. Ask for `ntpstat` / `timedatectl` output.
Maria Chen: customer ran `timedatectl` — output shows their clock advanced by ~2m twice around 20:55 and 21:02. They have an internal cron that runs `ntpdate pool.ntp.org` every few mins.
Priya Shah: that pattern would cause some events to appear with future timestamps, then after clockjump back, the agent might treat them as stale relative to control-plane wall time and drop them due to `offline_flush.max_age`.
Priya Shah: can you run these repro commands on the host (no-prod) and share results?
Priya Shah: ```
sudo journalctl -u redwood-meter-agent -n 300 --no-pager | grep -E "buffer_flush|drop_event|heartbeat"
sudo du -sh /var/lib/redwood/meter
ntpstat || timedatectl status
rd-meterctl inspect --agent agent-7b3c --since 3h
```
Devon R.: meanwhile I want to verify ledger vs audit. Maria, can you export the agent's local ledger snapshot and a short window from the control-plane ledger for 2026-02-12T20:30..21:30?
Maria Chen: exporting now. Note: customer VM had /var mounted on small disk. The agent rotated and removed older segments. I see a local replay file named `queue-20260212-2002.seg` but the later segments are missing.
Oncall SRE: I pulled the control-plane ingestion logs: got a replay marker for agent-7b3c at 2026-02-12T21:04:01 but there are gaps between 20:58..21:02 where no events arrived.
Kevin Liu: that matches disk-full window. Two effects possible: 1) agent buffered events locally, then disk filled and older segments got evicted leading to lost events; 2) clock jumps made some buffered events exceed retention and agent deleted them during cleanup.
Priya Shah: short-term mitigation: increase `offline_flush.max_age` to 60m and raise `persistent_queue.min_free_space` to 500MB so agent stops evicting when disk is tight. Also add a backoff to ntp cron. We'll push patch 1.4.3 with safer defaults.
Devon R.: for billing reconciliation we need an auditable delta. Steps:
Devon R.: 1) compute sum(tokens) from control-plane ledger for agent-7b3c for time range. 2) compute sum of audit logs emitted by customer app (if they have request-side logs). 3) check local agent ledger segments we still have and replay dry-run to count tokens that never made it to control-plane.
Devon R.: example query we ran on control-plane for that agent: ```
SELECT SUM(tokens) FROM meter_events WHERE agent_id='agent-7b3c' AND ts >= '2026-02-01' AND ts < '2026-02-13';
-- result: 1,150,234
```
Maria Chen: customer provided app-side totals: 1,170,000 tokens (their internal proxy traced tokens per request). Dashboard shows 1,032,110.
Priya Shah: so control-plane has 1,150k, app has 1,170k, dashboard 1,032k. Looks like about 117k events were never ingested to the dashboard but some did make it to the billing ledger. Possible explanations: double-counting at billing side (replayed events counted twice), or dashboard aggregation window missed late-arriving events.
Kevin Liu: check dedup keys. The agent attaches `event_id` and we dedupe on ingest. If agent replayed the same events twice after reconnect, the ledger could have replay markers but dedupe should prevent duplicates; check `ingest_replay_count` metrics.
Oncall SRE: ingest metrics show a small spike in `replay_ingests` at 21:04 with `replay_batch_count=4` and `ingest_replay_duplicates=0`.
Devon R.: run this to simulate replay from existing segments (dry-run): ```
rd-meter-replay --path /var/lib/redwood/meter/queue --agent agent-7b3c --dry-run --count-tokens
# prints total tokens in remaining segments
```
Maria Chen: dry-run shows 18,453 tokens in remaining segments. So lost segments likely contained the missing ~117k.
Priya Shah: action items:
- immediate: ask customer to free up disk or mount larger volume and upgrade to 1.4.3 candidate (config tweaks). I'll open PR with defaults. :thumbsup:
- reconciliation: SRE/ billing to compute final invoiced tokens vs control-plane ledger and apply credit if over-billed. Devon, Kevin to own.
- postmortem: collect agent configs, host disk rotation policy, ntp cron, and exact segment deletions.
Kevin Liu: I'll prepare a script to compute per-agent delta and generate a CSV for billing reconciliation.
Devon R.: assign support ticket 78912 to billing-team and tag for manual credit review. Also schedule follow-up with customer next Tuesday.
Maria Chen: customer agreed to increase disk and will pause aggressive ntp cron.
Oncall SRE: putting monitoring warnings to ensure `persistent_queue.free_space` alert thresholds trigger earlier.
Priya Shah: long-term: switch to write-ahead store with checksum+cloud-archive so we can recover buffered events even when local evictions happen.
Maria Chen: thanks everyone. I'll update the support ticket with logs, the dry-run count, and next steps.
Kevin Liu: thanks — :eyes:
meter-agent-bot: NOTE scheduled job: deploy 1.4.3-candidate to staging with buffer-retention changes on 2026-02-15 02:00 UTC :rocket:
Priya Shah: leaving this thread open for postmortem notes and the reconciliation CSV.
